links.targetTitle: The Integration Boost verifies submitted data against on-cha

title: Integration Boost net deposit data must be on-chain verifiable, and is currently produced by the Core Council Risk Advisor at a named external API
content:
A.2.2.9.2.2.1.2.1 sets the standard and then the implementation. The standard: "Integration Boost Partners must submit net deposit data in such a form that the data can be verified by Sky using on-chain data." The implementation: "In the short term, the Core Council Risk Advisor calculates the net deposit data based on on-chain events and makes it available to Operational GovOps through an API endpoint," with two specific `info-sky.blockanalitica.com` URLs named for Ethereum and Solana partners.

Two things are notable. First, the Atlas — a constitutional document — contains live third-party HTTP endpoints as operative content, which makes an external service's availability and correctness part of the governance substrate rather than an implementation detail. Second, the party computing the data today is the Core Council Risk Advisor, not the partner who is nominally obliged to submit it, so the stated obligation is currently discharged on the partner's behalf.

The long-term intent shifts responsibility rather than removing it: "Operational GovOps assumes responsibility for ensuring that the data submission meets the on-chain verifiability requirement; this is done as part of their review of Invocations of the Integration Boost Primitive." Verification moves from a central data provider to per-Invocation review by each Agent's Executor — consistent with the Atlas's general direction of pushing operations to Executors.

A.2.2.9.2.2.1.2.2 makes the same migration explicit for submission: the responsible party is the Core Council Risk Advisor near term, and long term "may be the Integration Boost Partner, a third party contractor, or the Prime Agent or Operational GovOps themselves if they agree to do so" — a set of options rather than an assignment.
description: The Atlas hardcodes two blockanalitica endpoints for Ethereum and Solana as the interim data source, with Operational GovOps assuming the verifiability duty long term.
